item.title: Departmental ministerial appointment
item.description: The Governor-General has accepted my recommendation to appoint Senator the Hon Tim Ayres, Minister for Industry and Innovation and Minister for Science, to administer the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (PM&C).This appointment reflects Minister Ayres’ role contributing to oversight of the Office of Artificial Intelligence, which is designing world-leading national AI standards to ensure Australians can share the benefits of this transformative technology, safely, and that AI works in Australia’s interests.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Press conference - Saint John's, Antigua and Barbuda
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: It's been a really productive day here at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting. CHOGM, of course, brings together 56 nations, representing a third of the world's population and representing a significant portion of the world's GDP. It, of course, has been concentrating on the issue of the global economy and international trade. And I've taken the opportunity to advance Australia's national interests, which is why we engage with our interconnected world.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Commonwealth Heads of Government 2026 statement between the UK and Australia
item.description: Addressing online violence in our democracies – promoting equality in Commonwealth Parliaments.A toxic online environment is a threat to all Commonwealth democracies. It threatens our values and undermines our people’s freedom and choices.  Workplace violence in any context is unacceptable, including that faced by journalists and media who are crucial to protecting freedom and democracy. We also condemn rising violence and aggression towards all frontline workers, including health and retail workers.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: CHOGM Joint Forums and side events official launch
item.description: Your Excellency Sir Rodney Williams, Governor-General of Antigua and Barbuda, and Lady Sandra Williams.The Right Honourable Gaston Browne, Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda, and Minister Maria Browne.Your Excellencies, Heads of Government and Heads of Delegation.The Honourable Shirley Botchwey, Commonwealth Secretary-General.It is a great pleasure to be here in Antigua and Barbuda.And to join friends from across the Commonwealth.This means friends from every continent, many cultures and multiple faiths.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Commonwealth Nature Initiative side event
item.description: The Right Honourable Gaston Browne, Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda.Your Excellencies, Heads of Government, Heads of Delegation, Honourable Ministers.Our host Dr Andrew Forrest.Business and nongovernment organisation leaders.It’s a pleasure to be here, on the Green Pioneer, for a green pioneer – to honour the environmental leadership of His Majesty The King.Protecting and restoring nature is a global, intergenerational compact.And that is the ambition at the heart of the Commonwealth Nature Initiative.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Press conference - Saint John's, Antigua and Barbuda
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: This morning I had the great honour of giving the keynote address at the opening of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting here in Antigua. The Commonwealth is an important institution of which Australia has played an important historical part. 56 countries representing one third of the world's population, 2.7 billion people. The combined economies will be pretty close to $30 trillion dollars next year. That represents a double of what it was just a decade ago.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: 2027 WA Australian of the Year Awards
item.description: What you see on this stage is the best of what being an Australian looks like.It is people who tell our national story through action.And they tell our national story through the compassion they have for Australians that they will probably never meet themselves.And a lot has changed over the last five years.But I've had the joy of being responsible for helping with the National Australia Day Council for five years, and something I learned really early on, which remains as true today as it was when I first learnt it.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting
item.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will travel to Antigua and Barbuda to attend the 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) from 31 October to 4 November 2026.Representatives from over 50 countries are expected to attend the meeting to discuss shared challenges and opportunities under the theme of Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth.The Commonwealth is a unique and diverse grouping of 56 countries, representing 2.7 billion people from both advanced and developing economies across the world.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Press conference - Canberra
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning. This has been a big week in parliament. Yesterday, the House of Representatives passed the Digital Duty of Care legislation. It is vital that this get the support of the Senate. It does two things essentially, the first is it makes big tech accountable. Just as the media organisations represented here are accountable for what’s on their platforms, they should be held to account for the role that they play and what appears on their platforms and which therefore then get circulated right around Australia.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: National Veteran Employment Awards
item.description: I begin by acknowledging the Traditional Owners of the land on which we meet and I pay my respects to their elders past, present and emerging.Thank you, Aunty Serena Williams, for that beautiful welcome to country.I’d like to acknowledge all our distinguished guests, including my colleagues from across the Parliament.I especially want to thank the veterans and serving personnel of the Australian Defence Force and the families who provide them with support.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: National Police Bravery Awards
item.description: I begin by acknowledging the Traditional Owners of the Land on which we meet, and I pay my respects to Elders past, present and emerging.I would also like to acknowledge:Scott Weber, CEO of the Police Federation of AustraliaKrissy Barrett, Commissioner of the AFPAnd all other distinguished guests, including my colleagues from across the Parliament.I would especially like to acknowledge all police officers here with us tonight – and on behalf of the nation, I thank you.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Veteran employment awards celebrate success beyond service
item.description: Supporting the long-term wellbeing of veterans and their families is a key focus of the Albanese Government.The Royal Commission into Defence and Veteran Suicide identified the transition from full-time ADF service to civilian life as a key pressure point for many in the veteran community.A good job with a supportive employer can ease that pressure and underpin a successful transition for veterans and families of veterans.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: The Australian Workers' Union 2026 National Conference
item.description: I begin by acknowledging the traditional owners of the land on which we meet and I pay my respects to their elders past, present, and emerging.To National Secretary, Paul Farrow, National President Marina Chambers, National Executive Members, Elected Delegates, and Rank and File Members.Thank you for this opportunity to acknowledge the great support of the AWU.Paul invited me personally and I was delighted to accept.It’s been a privilege to get to know Paul in recent years.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Digital duty of care
item.description: Well, thanks very much, Mr. Speaker.For several years now, Australians have been increasingly concerned about the impact of the online world on the welfare of children and on the cohesiveness of our society.A movement for change, begun and led by brave parents who saw their children's lives taken by cruel and highly addictive social media, created a remarkable period of bipartisanship that put Australia in the forefront of global movements to bring about online safety.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Western Sydney goes international
item.description: The first international arrival to Australia’s newest full-service airport has touched down, with Air New Zealand NZ165 from Auckland landing at Western Sydney International (Nancy-Bird Walton) Airport earlier this morning.After a short stopover, a full flight was boarded for the return leg and NZ166 departed. This is the first of three weekly return flights between Western Sydney International Airport (WSI) and New Zealand’s largest city.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Helen Haines - Parliament House, Canberra
item.description: As the House meets for the first time since the horrific events of last Monday, it is appropriate that our very first act is to speak about the Member for Indi, Dr Helen Haines.Her husband, Phil Haines, is with us this morning. He has shown a level of grace that, for most of us, is simply beyond reckoning.This morning Phil spoke lovingly of Helen’s superpowers as empathy, kindness and compassion.He spoke of hope and change, and the need for a gentler, more cohesive path.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Hellenic Club Centenary Gala Ball
item.description: I begin by acknowledging the Traditional Owners of the land on which we meet, and pay my respects to Elders past, present and emerging.I would also like to thank your President, Nick Hazistergos, for asking me to be part of this landmark moment in the Hellenic Club’s history.It is such a joy to be with you tonight to celebrate 100 years of the Hellenic Club, Sydney.To crack a century is never a matter of mere luck.The Hellenic Club is a story written in the ink of belief, determination and hard work – by many people over many generations.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Opening of Western Sydney International Airport
item.description: I begin by acknowledging the Traditional Owners of the land on which we meet, and I pay my respects to Elders past, present and emerging.I’d like to thank and Wurundjeri Elder Jason Tweedie for the smoking ceremony, and John Terrick for that wonderful yidaki performance.I would also like to acknowledge Her Excellency Governor Margaret Beazley, Western Sydney International chair Paul O’Sullivan, Western Sydney CEO Simon Hickey, Premier Chris Minns, and all my colleagues from across federal and state parliaments, past and present.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: First passengers lift off from WSI
item.description: At 11am Australian Eastern Daylight Time, JQ362 will take off from Western Sydney International (Nancy-Bird Walton) Airport, the first passenger flight for this brand new Airport.Hundreds of spectators will also be in attendance as the full capacity Jetstar Airbus A320 takes off for the maiden passenger voyage, connecting Western Sydney to the Gold Coast for the first time.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Australia's first major new airport has been decades in the making
item.description: This weekend, history will be made in Western Sydney.On Sunday, the first domestic flight will take off from Western Sydney International Airport. And on Monday, the first international flight will do the same.For the first time in more than 50 years, Australia is opening a major new airport.It’s a milestone that has been decades in the making and one that belongs to the people of Western Sydney.For generations, Western Sydney has been a place where people come to build a better life for themselves and their families.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Future Brisbane
item.description: Well, thanks very much, Jonesy, for the invitation to celebrate with you 10 years, a whole decade of dealing with Future Brisbane and being such a strong advocate for this great city and the way that the Courier Mail plays such a strong role.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Funding for world-class Gold Coast sports facility
item.description: The Gold Coast will be home to a new world-class facility with a strong focus on supporting women, girls and Para-athletes while creating a sporting legacy for the city.The Gold Coast Titans Community Hub and High Performance Centre in Carrara will bring the NRL and NRLW programs and Titans Netball together in one location, while opening up new facilities for community sport.The Albanese Government will invest $15 million towards the new centre, which will help grow junior participation and strengthen pathways from community sport to elite competition.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Radio interview - ABC Sydney
item.description: HAMISH MACDONALD, HOST: The Prime Minister, Anthony Albanese, is here to talk to you this morning. Good morning, PM.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning, Hamish. Good to be with you.MACDONALD: Obviously, we've had that update from Phil Haines. Do you have anything additional you can let us know about with regards to Helen's condition this morning?
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Radio interview - Nova Perth
item.description: NAT LOCKE, HOST: Prime Minister, good morning.SHAUN MCMANUS, HOST: Good morning, Albo.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning. Good to be with you.LOCKE: You too. I saw that you were in Perth over the weekend for Telethon.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Radio interview - ABC Perth
item.description: MARK GIBSON, HOST: You never quite know who's going to phone into the breakfast show. Line two, the Prime Minister, Anthony Albanese. Good morning.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning, Mark. 2008, it doesn't seem like that long ago.GIBSON: It doesn't, does it? 16 years ago.PRIME MINISTER: Yeah.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Radio interview - 2SM Sydney
item.description: CHRIS SMITH, HOST: On the line right now I've got the Prime Minister, Anthony Albanese. PM, welcome to the show.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning, Chris. Good to be with you.SMITH: You would have been listening at least to some of that press conference yesterday. Heartbreaking to hear that she had lost her second leg as well. And she really is in for the fight of her life from here, isn't she?
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: We need only look to Helen Haines
item.description: In too many ways, the world is a more dangerous and divided place than it was a generation ago.And often as Australians when we see political violence elsewhere we take pride and comfort in the idea that our democracy is differentMore peaceful, more stable, more respectful.This is why the horrific attack on Helen Haines has so shocked our nation.This was an attack on a hardworking, intelligent and thoroughly decent woman who is beloved in her community – and respected across the Parliament.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Television interview - News24
item.description: KIERAN GILBERT, HOST: It's been a very tough week for the town of Wangaratta, for the Parliament of the nation, and of course, for the family of Helen Haines as she continues to fight for her life in a Melbourne hospital. To discuss this and all the ramifications of this alleged act of violence against an MP, let's bring in Prime Minister Anthony Albanese. PM, thanks very much for your time. Have you got an update on Helen today?
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Radio interview - ABC Melbourne
item.description: RAF EPSTEIN, HOST: The Prime Minister Anthony Albanese joins us on the line. Good morning, PM.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning, Raf. Good to be with you.EPSTEIN: Have you spoken to Helen Haines or Helen Haines’ family recently, yesterday or today?
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Speech - The Age's Melbourne Assembly
item.description: I begin by acknowledging the traditional owners of the land on which we meet and I pay my respects to their elders past, present and emerging.Thank you to Neary Ty for the warm introduction.I acknowledge the Premier of Victoria, my friend Ben Carroll.Ben takes a huge amount of pride in his city and his state.He knows the suburbs and the regions, and he advocates and delivers for them.Ben and his Government believe in this great state, and in its ability to continue to grow and thrive and lead the nation into the future, right across the board.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Television interview - ABC News Breakfast
item.description: JAMES GLENDAY, HOST: We are now joined by the Prime Minister, Anthony Albanese, who is in Sydney for us this morning. Prime Minister, welcome back to News Breakfast.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning, James.GLENDAY: Really appreciate you making time for us. Is there anything at all you can tell us about the state of this investigation and also the condition of Helen Haines?
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Television interview - News24
item.description: PETER STEFANOVIC, HOST: Prime Minister, good to have you with us this morning. Thanks for your time. Do you have any more information on the attack this morning?
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Television interview - Today Show
item.description: SYLVIA JEFFREYS, HOST:  It is being described as one of the darkest days in Australian political history. Federal Independent MP Helen Haines struck by a car outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, in what's suspected to be a targeted attack.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Television interview - Sunrise
item.description: DAVID WOIWOD, HOST: Joining us now is Prime Minister Anthony Albanese. Good morning to you, Prime Minister. Of course, our thoughts are with Helen Haines and her family this morning. Do you have any update on her condition?
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Television interview - ABC 7.30
item.description: SARAH FERGUSON, HOST: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese joins me now in the studio. Prime Minister, welcome.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good evening.FERGUSON: What's the very latest you know about Helen and how she is?
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Press conference - Sydney
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good evening. Tonight, I want to update Australians on a serious incident that has occurred in Victoria. This afternoon, Helen Haines, the Member for Indi, was attacked outside her electorate office in Wangaratta. All of our thoughts are with Helen, her family, her friends, her team, and her community at this extremely difficult time. We are praying for her full recovery. I want to thank the first responders for their extraordinary work. There is a major police investigation underway, and I can confirm that a suspect is in custody.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: 2026 Telethon gala ball
item.description: It is wonderful to be back here again at Telethon.I begin by acknowledging the Traditional Owners of the land on which we're meeting, and pay my respect to Elders, past, present, and emerging.I acknowledge too, the most important people who are involved in tonight's event and the events over the next 36 hours  – the kids we're helping, represented by the fabulous little stars that we saw before in the video, Aidan, Olivia, and Paige.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Albanese Government delivers $6 million to Telethon
item.description: The Albanese Government has committed $6 million to the Channel 7 Telethon Trust for 2026 to help improve the health and wellbeing of Australian babies and children.Telethon is an annual televised fundraising appeal in Western Australia and is broadcast live for 26 hours.For almost six decades, Telethon has raised more than $778 million for sick and disadvantaged children in Western Australia.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Centenary of parliament sitting
item.description: To mark 100 years since our national parliament first met in Canberra, the 48th Australian Parliament will sit for a day at Old Parliament House in April next year.The special sitting day will see Question Time, legislation and other statements return to the Chambers of Old Parliament House for the first time in decades.In 1927, the “Provisional Parliament” was opened in Canberra and our national parliamentarians continued to meet in that building until 1988.Learning from our democratic history and institutions is more important than ever.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Centenary of the Canberra Times
item.description: Thank you so much, JP.I also join in acknowledging the Traditional Owners of the Land on which we meet, and I pay my respects to Elders past, present and emerging, as well as to all First Nations people with us here this evening.To the Governor-General, Your Excellency, it is wonderful to be with you as well.And I think you are doing an extraordinary job, and I say, more than fulfilling the confidence that I had in you.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Federation of Ethnic Communities' Councils of Australia national conference
item.description: Thank you so much to Prerana and to Peter for giving us a powerful beginning for this morning's events and discussions. And thank you to Auntie Serena and her niece and nephew for once again giving us a wonderful Welcome to Country. And I join with her in acknowledging the traditional owners of the land on which we're meeting, past, present and emerging. I acknowledge Dr Anne Aly, our fantastic Minister for Multicultural Affairs, and I acknowledge other Members of Parliament, Senators who are here, and I thank all the sponsors who are here as well, who of course make this possible.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Opening remarks - Parliament House, Canberra
item.description: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER OF AUSTRALIA: Your Majesty, it is an absolute honour to welcome you to Australia. We had a very good meeting last year in New York, where we discussed the full range of issues confronting not just our nations, but confronting the world and humanity. Unfortunately, some of those are of course, still going because we do live in a time of increasing global uncertainty, particularly with the escalating conflict in the Middle East. We share your condemnation of the Houthi attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Joint leaders' Statement on Enhanced Cooperation
item.description: The Prime Minister of Australia, the Hon Anthony Albanese MP, and His Majesty King Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan met in Canberra on 14 October 2026 and reaffirmed the enduring friendship between Australia and Jordan built on mutual respect and a shared commitment to peace, security and prosperity. Leaders welcomed the opportunity to set a forward-looking agenda for strengthened cooperation, building on the 2016 Joint Declaration on Enhanced Cooperation, and reflecting the growing breadth of the bilateral relationship.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Television interview - ABC Afternoon Briefing
item.description: PATRICIA KARVELAS, HOST: The Prime Minister is my lead guest this afternoon, Anthony Albanese, Welcome to the program.ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Goood afternoon. Good to be with you.KARVELAS: In the last couple of weeks, some Labor MPs have been feeling a little bit nervous. Today you told your Caucus you would be kicking with the wind in the fourth quarter. It's a term you used before the last election I recall –PRIME MINISTER: And the one before.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Visit to Australia by the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan
item.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will welcome His Majesty King Abdullah II ibn Al Hussein of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan to Australia from 13 to 14 October 2026.Australia and Jordan share a warm relationship, underpinned by defence and security cooperation.Our countries are working together to advance peace and regional security, support humanitarian efforts, to counter terrorism and violent extremism, to grow trade and to strengthen cooperation on resources, energy, and the environment.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: National reflection 25 years of Australian service in Afghanistan
item.description: It is a profound honour to join with you today on this landmark anniversary.I acknowledge Her Excellency, the Governor-General of Australia, Sam Mostyn, I acknowledge the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence, Richard Marles, and the Minister for Veterans' Affairs, Matt Keogh. I acknowledge the Leader of the Opposition, and other parliamentarians who are here. I acknowledge former prime ministers' John Howard, Tony Abbott and Scott Morrison.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: 25 years since Australians answered the call in Afghanistan
item.description: Today marks 25 years since the commencement of Operation Slipper, Australia’s first military contribution to the war in Afghanistan and the beginning of a significant chapter in our nation’s military history.  In the wake of the 11 September 2001 terrorist attacks in the United States, Australia joined an international coalition to combat terrorism and support security and stability in Afghanistan.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Vale Richard Morecroft
item.description: I was very sorry to hear of the passing of Richard Morecroft. As the face and the voice of the news of the ABC, Richard became a beloved part of Australian life. Combining a consummate professionalism with an unyielding humanity, Richard was a figure of absolute trust, a warm and familiar presence who guided us through the good times and bad.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Third anniversary of October 7 attacks
item.description: Today, we pause to remember the devastation that Hamas unleashed in the terrorist attack in Israel on the 7th of October, 2023. On this dark anniversary, we remember the 1200 who were taken from the world, the largest loss of Jewish life on any single day since the Holocaust.We think of everyone who was dragged into captivity, everyone who never returned home to their families, and everyone forever scarred by what they endured.
item.dc:creator: PMC

item.title: Statement on Death of Australian Army Soldier
item.description: Our nation’s thoughts are with the family, friends and colleagues of the Australian Army soldier who has tragically died during a training exercise in the Northern Territory yesterday.  Our thoughts are also with the five other Australian Army soldiers who were injured in the incident, and we wish them a speedy recovery. There are no safe or easy days for those who serve in our country's name. This sad incident is a terrible reminder of what families take on when their loved one bravely puts on our nation's uniform.
item.dc:creator: PMC
